issue.body:

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Fixed reading Parquet arrays of tuples when none of the requested tuple elements is in the file, e.g. a field added to a struct inside an array by schema evolution: such arrays were read as empty, so `ARRAY JOIN` and filters on their size lost rows. Now they keep their sizes from the file, and the missing elements get default values.


### Description

On 26.10.3.7, with a file written as `l Array(Tuple(a Int32, c String))`, `SELECT l.d FROM file('f.parquet', Parquet, 'l Array(Tuple(a Int32, c String, d Nullable(Int32)))')` returns `[]` instead of `[NULL]`, `ARRAY JOIN l.d` drops every row, `WHERE length(l.d) > 0` matches nothing, inserting `l.a, l.d` into a `Nested` column fails with `SIZES_OF_ARRAYS_DONT_MATCH`, and the structure `l Array(Tuple(d Nullable(Int32)))` reads `[]`. Reading the whole `l` keeps the sizes. Iceberg reaches this through schema evolution of a struct inside a list; there the whole column is fixed, while its subcolumns read `[]` for another reason (#130023).

Parquet stores array sizes (repetition/definition levels) only in leaf columns, and the reader requested a leaf only for requested elements that exist in the file, so nothing under the array was read.

Now, when no requested element under an array has a leaf, the reader also reads one leaf of the array only for its levels (preferring a fixed-width leaf, even one read for another column), and fills the missing elements with defaults per element. This covers the whole column, `arr.elem` subcolumns and flattened subcolumns like `l.d`, at any array depth. A column like `l.d` that is not in the file is still reported as missing, so its `DEFAULT` applies. An array dropped from the Iceberg schema is never used, and an ambiguous case-insensitive match fails with `DUPLICATE_COLUMN`. A leaf that cannot be decoded raises the error it raises when requested. Its values are dropped right after decoding, and the columns cache key tells such a column apart.

`03548_parquet_missing_tuple_elements` pinned the empty arrays; two of its expectations change, and it is extended with ARRAY JOIN, WHERE, PREWHERE, a `DEFAULT`, nested arrays, a `GEOMETRY` leaf, Iceberg schema changes, the columns cache and case-insensitive matching. It fails on master and passes with the fix. ORC is not changed here.

🕵 A note on how the readers should be unified later, from fixing the same shape for ORC in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130279 (kept ORC-local there because it needs a backport).

The Arrow reader (the by-name block in the struct read of `ArrowColumnToCHColumn.cpp`), the ORC reader (`matchORCTupleElementsByName` in #130279) and the Parquet `SchemaConverter` each implement the same rule: named tuple elements are matched by name, requested elements that are not in the file get defaults, and the others are dropped. The copies exist only because `CAST` (`FunctionCast::createTupleWrapper`) converts named tuples that have no element names in common by position.

Suggested unification:
- An internal flag in `FunctionConvertSettings` (not a user setting, included in `updateHash`) that disables that positional fallback for named tuples, passed through `castColumn` and `createInternalCast`, and always set by `castColumnToRequestedType`, which Arrow, ORC and DWARF use.
- Then delete the Arrow and ORC copies, and use the same cast for the conversions inside the readers: ORC map keys, `Variant` branches, and the `Nested` element before `createNested`.
- What stays per format is keeping the sizes of lists and maps whose element struct has none of the requested fields: levels-only columns here, and in ORC its narrowest field read without converting its values.
- Choose the defaults for missing elements once: `CAST` uses `createColumn()->cloneResized`, which gives an `Enum` the invalid value 0, while #130279 uses `insertManyDefaultsInto`, which gives its first value.

comment.body: 🕵 Root cause is Docker Desktop, not ClickHouse: on bind mounts, Docker Desktop's file sharing implemented `renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE)` as a plain overwrite, so exchanging two metadata files destroyed one of them (https://github.com/docker/for-mac/issues/7687). issue.title: [C++][FlightRPC] gRPC transport casts Arrow structs to pb::FlightData
issue.body:
### Describe the bug, including details regarding any error messages, version, and platform.

`WritePayload()` and `ReadPayload()` in `cpp/src/arrow/flight/transport/grpc/serialization_internal.cc` pass a `FlightPayload` or `internal::FlightData` to gRPC through `reinterpret_cast<pb::FlightData*>`, and `SerializationTraits<pb::FlightData>` in `customize_grpc.h` casts it back. The object is not a `pb::FlightData`, so this is undefined behavior, and Clang CFI (`-fsanitize=cfi-unrelated-cast`) rejects it.

We found this in ClickHouse, which embeds Arrow and is enabling Clang CFI in its release builds. It reproduces on upstream `main`: built with `-flto=thin -fwhole-program-vtables -fvisibility=hidden -fsanitize=cfi -fno-sanitize-trap=cfi -fsanitize-recover=cfi`, `arrow-flight-test` reports one violation per cast site, plus one in gRPC's `call_op_set.h` on the same object:

    serialization_internal.cc:220:25: runtime error: control flow integrity check for type 'arrow::flight::protocol::FlightData' failed during cast to unrelated type

With CFI in trap mode, any Flight RPC that sends or receives `FlightData` aborts.

### Component(s)

C++, FlightRPC

issue.title: Azure opt-in marker changes disk identity across sessions, breaking re-ATTACH

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Object-storage disk layer: DiskObjectStorage, metadata storage adapters, transaction support for ...

issue.body:
### Describe what's wrong

- A dynamic disk using `from_env`/`from_zk`/`include` gets an Azure server-credentials marker regardless of its type or credentials.
- Re-ATTACH or re-CREATE of such a disk from a session with a different `s3_allow_server_credentials_in_user_queries` value changes its hash-derived identity.
- Named disks then fail with BAD_ARGUMENTS as already configured, and unnamed disks silently get a new `__tmp_internal_<hash>` disk.
- Affects master only, gated by `dynamic_disk_allow_*` settings, and also hits `clickhouse-local`.

Root cause: `DiskFromAST.cpp:225-226` appends the Azure marker whenever `has_include` or `has_substituted_value` is set, before checking whether the disk is actually Azure or uses server credentials. `has_substituted_value` is set for a substitution on any key, so even disks with explicit `account_name`/`account_key` get marked and hashed differently depending on the session setting.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `MergeTreeSettings::resolveDiskSetting` (MergeTreeSettings.cpp:3397) -> `DiskFromAST::createCustomDisk` runs `ServerCredentialMarkerInjector` on every non-attach resolution (user `CREATE`, full or short `ATTACH`, `ALTER ... MODIFY SETTING disk`) -> DiskFromAST.cpp:225-226 appends the marker -> `getOrCreateCustomDisk` hashes the marked definition into the disk name (DiskFromAST.cpp:102) and rejects a different hash for an existing name (DiskFromAST.cpp:125).

Affected locations:
- [`src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp:225`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/41e654b5d25dce/src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp#L225) — marker pushed for any disk with include/from_env/from_zk when the session is unrestricted
- [`src/Disks/getDiskConfigurationFromAST.cpp:145`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/41e654b5d25dce/src/Disks/getDiskConfigurationFromAST.cpp#L145) — has_substituted_value set for a substitution on any key
- [`src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp:102`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/41e654b5d25dce/src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp#L102) — unnamed disk name = hash of the (marked) definition
- [`src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/MetadataStorageFactory.cpp:144`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/41e654b5d25dce/src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/MetadataStorageFactory.cpp#L144) — local metadata directory is disks/<disk name>/

Impact: Tables on dynamic disks that use `from_env`/`from_zk`/`include` (gated by `dynamic_disk_allow_*`, off by default): `DETACH`/`ATTACH`, or sharing a named disk, across sessions whose `s3_allow_server_credentials_in_user_queries` differs is refused, and an unnamed object-storage disk is silently swapped for a new one. Enabling the setting for users who already own such tables, the migration #120343 recommends, triggers it, as does `clickhouse-local`, which is never restricted.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

No — only `master` (`41e654b5d25d`). The bug starts with #120343 (merged as `dccf74c0fd4a`), which is in no release yet, so a release build (and ClickHouse Fiddle) still passes.

### How to reproduce

Requires `USE_AZURE_BLOB_STORAGE` and `dynamic_disk_allow_from_env=1`; use `common_key_prefix_for_azure = 'from_env PATH'` with explicit `account_name`/`account_key`.

```bash
# Tag no-fasttest: needs USE_AZURE_BLOB_STORAGE.
# A dynamic disk with a `from_env` value and explicit credentials keeps its identity whatever the
# `s3_allow_server_credentials_in_user_queries` of the session that reuses or re-attaches it.

KEY="Eby8vdM02xNOcqFlqUwJPLlmEtlCDXJ1OUzFT50uSRZ6IFsuFq2UVErCz4I6tq/K1SZFPTOtr/KBHBeksoGMGw=="
# `readonly`, `container_already_exists` and `skip_access_check` keep the disk from contacting the endpoint.
ARGS="type = azure_blob_storage, storage_account_url = 'https://localhost:11111/devstoreaccount1',
    container_name = 'cont${CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE//_/}', account_name = 'devstoreaccount1', account_key = '${KEY}',
    readonly = 1, container_already_exists = 1, skip_access_check = 1, common_key_prefix_for_azure = 'from_env PATH'"
NAMED="disk(name = 'disk_default', ${ARGS})"
UNNAMED="disk(${ARGS})"

OPT_IN="--s3_allow_server_credentials_in_user_queries=1"

run() {
    local out
    if out=$(clickhouse-client --dynamic_disk_allow_from_env=1 "$@" 2>&1); then echo "OK"; else echo "$out" | grep -oE '\([A-Z_]+\)' | head -1; fi
}

clickhouse-client -q "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_named; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_named_2; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_unnamed"

run -q "CREATE TABLE t_named (x UInt8) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() SETTINGS disk = ${NAMED}" > /dev/null
echo "same named disk, session with the opt-in: $(run ${OPT_IN} -q "CREATE TABLE t_named_2 (x UInt8) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() SETTINGS disk = ${NAMED}")"

clickhouse-client -q "DETACH TABLE t_named"
echo "re-attach, session without the opt-in: $(run -q "ATTACH TABLE t_named")"
clickhouse-client -q "DETACH TABLE t_named"
echo "re-attach, session with the opt-in: $(run ${OPT_IN} -q "ATTACH TABLE t_named")"

run -q "CREATE TABLE t_unnamed (x UInt8) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple() SETTINGS disk = ${UNNAMED}" > /dev/null
before=$(clickhouse-client -q "SELECT data_paths FROM system.tables WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND name = 't_unnamed'")
clickhouse-client -q "DETACH TABLE t_unnamed"
run ${OPT_IN} -q "ATTACH TABLE t_unnamed" > /dev/null
after=$(clickhouse-client -q "SELECT data_paths FROM system.tables WHERE database = currentDatabase() AND name = 't_unnamed'")
echo "unnamed disk kept after re-attach with the opt-in: $([ "$before" = "$after" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"

clickhouse-client -q "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_named; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_named_2; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t_unnamed"
```

Verified: this block reproduces on current `master` (`41e654b5d25d`) when pasted as is.

### Expected behavior

The custom disk's name and identity should stay the same regardless of the session's `s3_allow_server_credentials_in_user_queries` value, as required by the invariant at DiskFromAST.cpp:99-101.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
same named disk, session with the opt-in: OK
re-attach, session without the opt-in: OK
re-attach, session with the opt-in: OK
unnamed disk kept after re-attach with the opt-in: 1
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

Named disk re-use or re-ATTACH from a session with a different setting value fails with BAD_ARGUMENTS, and an unnamed disk gets silently replaced with a new `__tmp_internal_<hash>` disk, moving `data_paths`.

Actual output of the reproducer above on `master` (`41e654b5d25d`):

```
same named disk, session with the opt-in: (BAD_ARGUMENTS)
re-attach, session without the opt-in: OK
re-attach, session with the opt-in: (BAD_ARGUMENTS)
unnamed disk kept after re-attach with the opt-in: 0
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Mark only disks the Azure restriction can apply to: an Azure backend (`getAzureDiskPrefixes` non-empty) or an indirect `type`/`object_storage_type`, and only when the substituted or included values can supply the endpoint or auth or no literal `account_key`/`connection_string` is present, like `persist_server_credentials_allowance` for S3. Trade-off: keep `include` conservative, since it can add keys the AST does not show; `validateResolvedAzureDiskCredentials` still re-checks after resolution.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- Not verified: `DatabaseReplicated` replicas that run the `CREATE` with clamped settings could compute a different disk name than the initiator for such definitions.

Introduced by [PR #120343](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/120343), found during its automated review: the reproducer passes on the master build just before it merged and fails on the build with it. Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr120343_001`

- Merged into: `26.11.1.1829-master` (included in `26.11` and later)

issue.title: `_server_credentials_allowed` changes the identity of a `disk(...)` declared before 26.7, so it can't be re-declared after an upgrade

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Core disk abstractions: IDisk interface, DiskLocal, storage policies, volumes, disk management to...

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Author is not a member of the ClickHouse organization

issue.body:
### Company or project name

Shopify

### Describe the unexpected behaviour

After upgrading from 26.3 to 26.8, a `disk(...)` declared before the upgrade can no longer be re-declared with the same text. Before the upgrade, the same `ATTACH` resolved to the existing disk.

A custom disk's identity is the `sipHash128` of its serialized definition. For an unnamed disk, the hash is the disk name. For a named disk, it is the stored settings hash ([DiskFromAST.cpp#L88-L100](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/v26.8.34.13-lts/src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp#L88-L100)).

Since 4992a4d5420 (#106855), `ServerCredentialMarkerInjector` appends `_server_credentials_allowed = 1` to leaf S3 disks that rely on server credentials, such as disks with `from_env` keys, when the session has `s3_allow_server_credentials_in_user_queries = 1` ([getDiskConfigurationFromAST.cpp#L261-L262](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/v26.8.34.13-lts/src/Disks/getDiskConfigurationFromAST.cpp#L261-L262)).
- The injector runs only `if (!attach)`, before flattening and hashing ([DiskFromAST.cpp#L247-L252](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/v26.8.34.13-lts/src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp#L247-L252)).
- A user `ATTACH TABLE`, full or short, is not a metadata load, so the injector runs there too ([registerStorageMergeTree.cpp#L881-L892](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/v26.8.34.13-lts/src/Storages/MergeTree/registerStorageMergeTree.cpp#L881-L892)).

A table created before 26.7 has no marker in its stored metadata. After an upgrade, the table loads from metadata without the injector, so its disk is registered under the old hash. Any user `CREATE` or `ATTACH` with the same `disk(...)` text then gets the marker and a different hash:
1. **Named disk** (here, the `cache` wrapper): the settings hash differs, so the query throws "already configured as a custom disk in another table" ([DiskFromAST.cpp#L117-L121](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/v26.8.34.13-lts/src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp#L117-L121)).
2. **Unnamed writable `s3_plain_rewritable` disk**: the new hash produces a new `__tmp_internal_<hash>` name. That registers a second plain-rewritable disk on the same prefix, which [DiskSelector.cpp#L50-L85](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/v26.8.34.13-lts/src/Disks/DiskSelector.cpp#L50-L85) rejects.

There seems to be no SQL workaround:
- The injector strips any marker the user writes before it decides whether to add one ([DiskFromAST.cpp#L214](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/v26.8.34.13-lts/src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp#L214)).
- Without the session setting, the definition is refused with `ACCESS_DENIED`.

Tables created on 26.7 or later store the marker and are not affected.

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?

- Affected:** tables created before 26.7, then used on 26.7 or later. The injector was first released in v26.7.1.1315-stable.
- **Tested:** 26.3.33.24 upgraded to 26.8.34.13, both official builds, on the same data directory.
- **Unchanged code on newer versions:** the hash, the mismatch check and the `if (!attach)` injection are the same on v26.10.2.103-stable and on master 230ae8eec3e ([DiskFromAST.cpp#L90](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/230ae8eec3e/src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp#L90), [#L122](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/230ae8eec3e/src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp#L122), [#L245](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/230ae8eec3e/src/Disks/DiskFromAST.cpp#L245)).


### How to reproduce

Server setup:**
- Point the environment variables at an S3/MinIO bucket:
  - `S3_ENDPOINT=http://<minio>:9000/<bucket>/data/`
  - `S3_KEY=<key>`
  - `S3_SECRET=<secret>`
- In config, set `<custom_cached_disks_base_directory>/var/lib/clickhouse/caches/</custom_cached_disks_base_directory>`.
- In the default profile, set `dynamic_disk_allow_from_env = 1`. On 26.8, also set `s3_allow_server_credentials_in_user_queries = 1`; otherwise the tables load anonymously or are refused.

**1. On 26.3:**

```sql
CREATE TABLE w (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x
SETTINGS table_disk = true, disk = disk(type = 's3_plain_rewritable',
    endpoint = 'from_env S3_ENDPOINT', access_key_id = 'from_env S3_KEY', secret_access_key = 'from_env S3_SECRET');
INSERT INTO w VALUES (1);

CREATE TABLE r (x UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x
SETTINGS table_disk = true, refresh_parts_interval = 1, disk = disk(name = 'r_cache', type = 'cache',
    path = '/var/lib/clickhouse/caches/r', max_size = '1Gi', disk = disk(type = 's3_plain_rewritable',
    endpoint = 'from_env S3_ENDPOINT', access_key_id = 'from_env S3_KEY', secret_access_key = 'from_env S3_SECRET', readonly = true));
```

**2. Restart on 26.8 with the same data directory.** `SELECT count() FROM r` and `SELECT count() FROM w` both return 1. Then bind a second table to each disk:

```sql
-- reader: same named cache disk
ATTACH TABLE r2 UUID '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001' (x UInt64, y String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x
SETTINGS table_disk = true, refresh_parts_interval = 1, disk = disk(name = 'r_cache', type = 'cache',
    path = '/var/lib/clickhouse/caches/r', max_size = '1Gi', disk = disk(type = 's3_plain_rewritable',
    endpoint = 'from_env S3_ENDPOINT', access_key_id = 'from_env S3_KEY', secret_access_key = 'from_env S3_SECRET', readonly = true));

-- writer: same unnamed plain-rewritable disk
ATTACH TABLE w2 UUID '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002' (x UInt64, y String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY x
SETTINGS table_disk = true, disk = disk(type = 's3_plain_rewritable',
    endpoint = 'from_env S3_ENDPOINT', access_key_id = 'from_env S3_KEY', secret_access_key = 'from_env S3_SECRET');
```

A `CREATE TABLE` with the reader disk fails the same way.

**Controls:**
- Both `ATTACH` statements succeed on 26.3, where they resolve to the existing disks.
- Tables created on 26.8 in another bucket also re-declare without error. Their stored disk contains `equals(_server_credentials_allowed, 1)`.


### Error message and/or stacktrace


issue.body:
### Describe the situation

Small edits rebuild far more than they need: each ClickHouse build reruns cargo and rewrites the Rust archives, so clickhouse relinks, and settings files and core headers pull thousands of files into the rebuild. These patches remove most of that work; precompiled headers speed up clean builds.

Median seconds from an edit (or empty tree) to a linked clickhouse, RelWithDebInfo: master + patch 1 vs patches 1–9, 2–3 interleaved pairs.

| Scenario | x86, 32 vCPU: before → after (s) | Change [95% CI] | ARM, 16 vCPU: before → after (s) | Change [95% CI] |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| No-op rebuild | 20.8 → 1.36 | **−93.4%** [−93.5%, −93.4%] | 23.5 → 1.76 | **−92.5%** [−93.1%, −92.0%] |
| Edit a leaf `.cpp` (getClusterName.cpp) | 23.5 → 11.8 | **−49.8%** [−52.2%, −48.6%] | 27.9* → 15.6 | **−44.1%** [−73.0%, −13.1%] |
| Edit `Settings.cpp` | 53.9 → 26.6 | **−50.7%** [−51.9%, −49.3%] | 71.0 → 34.6 | **−51.2%** [−51.8%, −50.8%] |
| Edit `ServerSettings.cpp` | 47.7 → 33.9 | **−28.9%** [−30.1%, −27.3%] | 60.2 → 44.5 | **−26.1%** [−29.2%, −24.5%] |
| Edit `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` | 39.9 → 19.6 | **−51.0%** [−52.4%, −48.9%] | 51.3 → 24.9 | **−51.5%** [−56.4%, −44.9%] |
| CMake re-run (touch `CMakeLists.txt`) | 34.1 → 9.60 | **−71.8%** [−76.8%, −68.2%] | 47.5* → 11.8 | **−75.2%** [−92.6%, −45.6%] |
| Edit `ProtocolDefines.h` | 311 → 155 | **−50.2%** [−51.0%, −49.3%] | 441 → 203 | **−53.9%** [−59.4%, −47.7%] |
| Edit `FormatSettings.h` | 1,546 → 440 | **−71.5%** [−71.5%, −71.5%] | 2,290 → 631 | **−72.4%** [−78.5%, −64.6%] |
| Edit `ISerialization.h` | 1,543 → 1,142 | **−26.0%** [−26.3%, −25.7%] | 2,324 → 1,678 | **−27.8%** [−33.1%, −22.1%] |
| New build directory, warm ccache | 437 → 275 | **−37.2%** [−41.3%, −32.7%] | 564 → 443 | **−21.5%** [−43.2%, +8.4%] |
| Clean build, empty ccache | 3,104 → 2,446 | **−21.2%** [−21.8%, −20.6%] | 4,641 → 3,689 | **−20.5%** [−25.5%, −15.2%] |

Before: master with patch 1, the link fix that master needed to link in these builds; after: all default-build patches (1–9). Change is the ratio of the medians; brackets give the 95% interval of the paired geometric-mean ratio. * On ARM the first master run after an idle period was slow (cold page cache: 42.3 s for the leaf edit, 93.0 s for the CMake re-run); the medians use all runs. Costs of the precompiled headers (patch 9) alone: a CMake re-run takes about 1 s longer (x86 8.6 → 9.5 s; ARM 10.8 → 12.2 s) and a new build directory with a warm ccache 4% longer on x86 (264.6 → 274.7 s; no measurable change on ARM), and 0.9 GB of PCH files in the build directory; with all patches applied no scenario got slower. Patch 10 adds an opt-in `-DSPLIT_DWARF=ON` (default off): on x86 a leaf edit took 13.0 → 10.1 s (−22%) and a `Settings.cpp` edit 43.4 → 40.1 s (−8%) compared with the same tree without it; split builds keep file and line in stack traces but show no inlined frames in-process (`addressToLineWithInlines` gave 45 frames for 45 stack addresses, against 118 in a default build).

<details><summary>What each patch changes, per-patch measurements and checks</summary>

1. **Link fix.** In our default RelWithDebInfo builds with clang/lld 21.1.8, master's `clickhouse` failed to link: `localize_rust_c_symbols.sh` rewrites the Rust archives with `llvm-objcopy` (`llvm-objcopy-21`, the `CMAKE_OBJCOPY` of these builds), which leaves `.llvm_addrsig` sections with `sh_link=0` in the objects where it localizes a symbol; lld's `--icf=safe` warns about them and `--fatal-warnings` fails the link. #126478 alone does not fix these builds: it makes CMake pass the LLVM objcopy instead of GNU objcopy, and these builds already used it. With `-Wl,--no-fatal-warnings` in the linker flags the link succeeds; we did not try CI's toolchain. The patch removes `.llvm_addrsig` there, as `strip_rust_symbols.sh` does since #122904; this works with GNU objcopy too. Patch 1 is a link fix that both measured trees contain; it is not measured on its own.
2. **Build system and settings.** Today every build runs the cargo builds and rewrites the copied Rust archives in place (`localize_rust_c_symbols.sh`, `strip_rust_symbols.sh`), so the copy never matches cargo's output, is rewritten again and `clickhouse` relinks even when nothing changed; every library linking a crate also waits for all cargo builds before compiling anything. The patch (a) runs each post-processing step as a custom command that writes a new archive only when its input changed (the approach of #119121); (b) builds the workspace crates with one `cargo build`, so they no longer wait for each other on cargo's target-directory lock, and skips cargo when no input of the Rust libraries changed (`cmake/cargo_if_changed.sh`, which checks cargo's dep-info files and falls back to running cargo); (c) links the crates through imported targets without the cargo dependency, so C++ compiles run in parallel with cargo and only the sources including `delta_kernel_ffi.hpp` wait for the delta-kernel build; (d) on a CMake re-run, rewrites configure-time generated files only when their content changes, lists licenses without a fork per vendored crate and keeps `git status` out of submodule work trees; (e) for the settings files, replaces per-setting template code with table-driven accessors in `BaseSettings.h` and shared field operations, includes `FormatFactorySettings.h` only where it is used and moves the disk checks of `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` to `MergeTreeSettingsDisks.cpp` (no more `MergeTreeData.h`, `ZooKeeper.h`, `ASTFunction.h`). Measured separately on x86, part (a) alone took the no-op rebuild from 21.1 to 4.4 s and the rest of the build-system changes to 1.3 s; part (e) alone took a `Settings.cpp` edit from 42.8 to 28.2 s. One `cargo build` for all workspace crates unifies the features of the dependencies they share, as `cargo build --workspace` does, so the linked Rust code changes slightly: on an earlier master this change alone made the binary 0.3 MB smaller, while the 136 exported Rust FFI symbols and the outputs of PRQL, polyglot, PCO and Vortex smoke queries stayed identical; skim and wasmtime were linked but not run.
3. **ProtocolDefines.h and friends.** The parallel-replicas protocol versions move to `ParallelReplicasProtocolDefines.h`, so `RequestResponse.h` (and everything including it) no longer depends on `ProtocolDefines.h`; `FileCachePolicy` moves to `Core/FileCachePolicy.h`, so `FileCache_fwd.h` no longer includes `SettingsEnums.h`; `ActionsDAG.h` and `IQueryPlanStep.h` are replaced by forward declarations where one suffices. A `ProtocolDefines.h` edit recompiles 115 files instead of 278.
4. **Direct includes.** 87 files that used `FormatSettings` (and a few other headers) through transitive includes include them directly. Patch 4 only adds the direct includes that patch 5 needs; it is not measured on its own.
5. **FormatSettings.h out of common headers.** `ReadHelpers.h`, `WriteHelpers.h`, `FormatFactorySettings.h`, `SettingsEnums.h` and `Context.h` included the whole `FormatSettings.h`. The CSV/JSON enums they need move to `FormatSettingsEnums.h` and the JSON number writers to `writeJSONNumber.h`/`WriteHelpers.cpp`: a `FormatSettings.h` edit recompiles 1,203 files instead of 3,222.
6. **FormatSettings.h out of the remaining wide headers.** `NativeWriter.h`, `DateTimeTransforms.h`, `FunctionBinaryArithmetic.h`, `convertFieldToType.h`, `convertColumnToType.h`, `VirtualColumnUtils.h` and a few others stop including it: 708 files instead of 1,203.
7. **Operators.h and IDataType.h.** `IO/Operators.h` no longer includes `IO/ReadHelpers.h` (a `ReadHelpers.h` edit: 1,338 files instead of 2,002, 1,147 → 933 s (−19%) when measured alone), and `IDataType.h` no longer includes `ISerialization.h`; the substream types it needs move to `SerializationSubstream.h` (an `ISerialization.h` edit: 2,286 files instead of 3,218, 1,516 → 1,267 s (−16%) alone).
8. **Unit-test include.** One unit test used `ISerialization.h` through `IDataType.h`. Patch 8 only adds an include to one unit test; it is not measured on its own.
9. **Precompiled headers.** `cmake/precompiled_headers.cmake` adds per-target PCHs of stable standard-library, fmt, magic_enum, `base/` and third-party headers to the 15 largest `src` targets and the largest contrib libraries, with `-fno-pch-timestamp` so ccache still hits in a new build directory. Earlier attempts found little gain: #9162 (2020) measured a clean build of 74 minutes with PCH against 76 without, and the `dbms`-only PCH listed in #96721 saved 5.9 s, about 3% of CPU time, at 192 cores. Patch 9 covers far more of the build, including the contrib sources that mostly parse their library headers: on these 16-core hosts it cut clean-build CPU time by 19% (x86) and 18% (ARM) and wall time by 18.8% and 17.5%, with the same `.text` size. Compiler caches stay correct: after a change of only the PCH content, sccache 0.19, chcache and ccache 4.9.1 all missed, because the headers inside the PCH are part of what each cache hashes; ccache gets the `pch_defines,time_macros` sloppiness it needs only for the targets with a PCH. We did not measure CI builds with sccache, where every fresh build directory builds the PCHs again.
10. **Opt-in SPLIT_DWARF.** A `SPLIT_DWARF` CMake option (`-gsplit-dwarf -gno-gnu-pubnames`) keeps most debug information out of the objects the linker reads. `Dwarf.cpp` accepts the skeleton units (`DW_TAG_skeleton_unit`) so stack traces keep file and line, and one test that reads the binary's DWARF is skipped in split builds, as it is for `-g0`.

Checks: master and patched binaries return identical `system.settings`, `system.server_settings`, `system.merge_tree_settings`, `system.licenses`, `system.formats`, `system.functions` and `system.table_engines`, sample values and Native output on both hosts; `system.build_options` differs only in the git fields. `unit_tests_dbms` passes with all patches on both hosts (x86: 30,289 tests, 25,497 passed, the rest skipped, none failed; ARM: 30,265 tests, 25,469 passed, 4,796 skipped, none failed, the same counts as master). Clean, new-directory and incremental builds all succeeded, every incremental scenario recompiled the edited file and relinked, and each binary answered a query. The binaries are not byte-identical: the header cuts move code between translation units, the single cargo build of patch 2 unifies Rust dependency features (see patch 2), and the PCHs change debug type information (with and without patch 9: same `.text`, `.rodata` and `.data` sizes on x86 and same `.text` size on ARM; `.debug_info` 3.6% (x86) and 3.8% (ARM) smaller from fewer duplicated type entries; equivalent symbolization of 3,000 sampled functions on ARM). On ARM, Time/DateTime conversions, uniqExact and general queries ran at the same speed with and without the patches (within ±0.7%, except a +1.8% uniqExact difference of the size that rebuilding identical sources also produces).

</details>

### Which ClickHouse versions are affected?

<details><summary>Tested versions and source commits</summary>

Measured on master 64576f956c6b (2026-11-03) with the patches applied in order. A three-way merge of the patches onto master 46ab3dad27eb (2026-11-07) conflicts only in `FormatSettings.h` and `ActionsDAG.cpp`, next to edited lines. Since the base, upstream changed only other lines of the build files these patches edit (source lists in `src/CMakeLists.txt`, OSS-Fuzz options in `CMakeLists.txt`), not the Rust, cargo, license or PCH steps. We did not rebuild on the newer master: new code that relies on an include these patches remove would need a direct include, as in patch 4.

</details>

### How to reproduce

<details><summary>Hosts, configuration and measurement procedure</summary>

- Hosts: x86, AWS r6i.8xlarge (16 cores / 32 vCPU, 247 GiB); ARM, AWS r7g.4xlarge (16 vCPU Graviton3, 123 GiB); Ubuntu 24.04.
- Toolchain: clang/lld 21.1.8 from apt.llvm.org, CMake 3.28.3, Ninja 1.11.1, ccache 4.9.1, Rust nightly-2026-03-22 as pinned by `contrib/corrosion-cmake`.
- Configuration (both arms): `cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang-21 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-21`, then `ninja -C build clickhouse` (default parallelism, ccache through `COMPILER_CACHE=auto`). Patch 10 is measured with `-DSPLIT_DWARF=ON` against the same tree without it.
- Trees: one source checkout and one `CCACHE_DIR` per arm, never shared. Before each incremental run the tree is synced with two no-op `ninja` runs.
- Scenarios, each timed from the edit to the finished `clickhouse` binary:
  - no-op: `ninja` on the synced tree;
  - leaf, `Settings.cpp`, `ServerSettings.cpp`, `MergeTreeSettings.cpp` and header edits: append a unique comment line to the file, `ninja`, then restore the file (the next sync rebuilds it);
  - CMake re-run: `touch CMakeLists.txt`, `ninja`;
  - new build directory with warm ccache: delete the build directory, `cmake` + `ninja`;
  - clean build: delete the build directory and the arm's ccache directory, `cmake` + `ninja`.
- Order: arms interleaved per scenario (A,B,B,A or A,B,B,A,A,B), 2 pairs for scenarios over 5 minutes, 3 for the others; the table shows medians and the 95% interval of the paired geometric ratio. The arm for patch 9 alone (all patches except 9 vs all patches) was interleaved with the same runs on x86.
- Patch application: 1 → 9 in order on master 64576f956c6b; patch 10 applies on top.

</details>

### Expected performance

<details><summary>Expected behavior</summary>

A rebuild should cost about as much as the change: no cargo run, archive rewrite or relink when no Rust input and no object changed; after a header edit, recompiling only the files that use the header; after a CMake re-run with no real change, no regenerated file that forces recompiles. Clean builds should not parse the same large third-party headers in every translation unit.

</details>

### Related issues and pull requests

<details><summary>Related work</summary>

- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/96721 collects build-speed work. Patches 3 and 5–7 cut transitive header dependencies so that a header edit recompiles fewer files, which Algunenano suggested there for local development; patch 9 extends the `dbms`-only PCH commit listed there (not merged) to per-target PCHs for the 15 largest `src` targets and the largest contrib libraries.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/9162 (2020, closed) tried CMake's precompiled headers and measured a clean build of 74 minutes with them against 76 without; the description of patch 9 says what differs here.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/122904 removed `.llvm_addrsig` in `strip_rust_symbols.sh`; patch 1 does the same in `localize_rust_c_symbols.sh`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126478 (open) fixes the same link error where CMake picks GNU objcopy, by passing the LLVM objcopy instead; patch 1 removes the section, so it also fixes builds like ours that already use `llvm-objcopy-21`, and the two changes do not conflict.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/124645 took the cargo builds out of Ninja's console pool; as it notes, the workspace crates still wait for each other on cargo's target-directory lock, which patch 2(b) removes by building them with one `cargo build`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/119121 by @al13n321 made the Rust archive post-processing incremental; it was closed without merging on 2026-10-29. Patch 2 contains that approach (part (a)), and our earlier measurements are in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/119121#issuecomment-6440742891.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/128815 (open) also changes `contrib/corrosion-cmake/CMakeLists.txt`: if it lands first, the single `cargo build` environment of patch 2 needs the same target-scoped `RUSTFLAGS`.
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/129767 and https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110548 (open), and draft https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/129961, add workspace crates. Their own steps rewrite Corrosion's copy of the archive in place: `strip_rust_symbols.sh`, and in #110548 also a localization of the lz4 and zstd symbols. With patch 2 the binaries link the post-processed archive of the single `cargo build` instead, so those steps would process a copy that is no longer linked. Whichever change lands second must turn them into `clickhouse_postprocess_rust_lib()` calls, as patch 2 does for prql, polyglot, pco and vortex.

</details>

### Additional context

Patches 1, 8, 9 and 10 are below; patches 2 to 7 follow in five comments because of GitHub's size limit (comment 1: patch 2; comment 2: patches 3 and 4; comment 3: patch 5; comment 4: patch 6; comment 5: patch 7).

**Patch 1: link fix for the localized Rust archives**

```diff
diff --git a/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh b/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
index 61cf95aa9c8..4ef48524c02 100755
--- a/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
+++ b/cmake/localize_rust_c_symbols.sh
@@ -125,12 +125,15 @@ if [ -s "$LOCALIZE_FILE" ]; then
     # Some Rust archives contain non-ELF members (e.g. debug metadata objects)
     # that cause llvm-objcopy to fail.  In that case, fall back to extracting
     # individual members, processing only valid ELF objects, and repacking.
-    if ! "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" "$LIB_PATH" 2>/dev/null; then
+    # Also drop .llvm_addrsig: objcopy leaves its sh_link at 0, and lld --icf=safe then warns that it ignores it

+    # when it ignores the table. See strip_rust_symbols.sh.
+    if ! "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" --remove-section=.llvm_addrsig "$LIB_PATH" 2>/dev/null; then
         WORK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
 
         (cd "$WORK_DIR" && "$AR" x "$LIB_PATH")
         for obj in "$WORK_DIR"/*.o; do
-            "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" "$obj" 2>/dev/null || true
+            "$OBJCOPY" --localize-symbols="$LOCALIZE_FILE" --remove-section=.llvm_addrsig "$obj" 2>/dev/null || true
         done

     fi
```

```diff
+function (clickhouse_target_precompiled_headers target)
+    cmake_parse_arguments (PCH "SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES" "REUSE_FROM" "HEADERS" ${ARGN})
+    if (PCH_REUSE_FROM)
+        target_precompile_headers (${target} REUSE_FROM ${PCH_REUSE_FROM})
+    else ()
+        set (headers)
+        foreach (header IN LISTS PCH_HEADERS)
+            list (APPEND headers "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:<${header}$<ANGLE-R>>")
+        endforeach ()
+        target_precompile_headers (${target} PRIVATE ${headers})
+    endif ()
+    # Keep template instantiation in the translation units, so the generated code does not change.
+    set_target_properties (${target} PROPERTIES PCH_INSTANTIATE_TEMPLATES OFF)
+
+    get_target_property (source_dir ${target} SOURCE_DIR)
+    get_target_property (binary_dir ${target} BINARY_DIR)
+    get_target_property (sources ${target} SOURCES)
+    foreach (source IN LISTS sources)
+        if (source MATCHES "^\\$<" OR NOT source MATCHES "\\.(cpp|cc|cxx)$")
+            continue ()
+        endif ()
+        # Resolve like CMake does: relative to the target's source directory, else its binary directory (generated files).
+        if (IS_ABSOLUTE "${source}")
+            set (path "${source}")
+        elseif (EXISTS "${source_dir}/${source}")
+            set (path "${source_dir}/${source}")
+        else ()
+            set (path "${binary_dir}/${source}")
+        endif ()
+        if (PCH_SKIP_TARGET_DIR_SOURCES)
+            string (FIND "${path}" "${source_dir}/" pos)
+            if (pos EQUAL 0)
+                set_source_files_properties ("${path}" TARGET_DIRECTORY ${target} PROPERTIES SKIP_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS ON)
+                continue ()
+            endif ()
+        endif ()
+        foreach (property COMPILE_FLAGS COMPILE_OPTIONS COMPILE_DEFINITIONS)
+            get_source_file_property (value "${path}" TARGET_DIRECTORY ${target} ${property})
+            if (value)
+                set_source_files_properties ("${path}" TARGET_DIRECTORY ${target} PROPERTIES SKIP_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS ON)
+                break ()
+            endif ()
+        endforeach ()
+    endforeach ()
+
+    get_target_property (launcher ${target} CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER)
+    list (FILTER launcher INCLUDE REGEX "(^|/)ccache$")
+    if (launcher)
+        execute_process (COMMAND ${launcher} --get-config sloppiness
+            OUTPUT_VARIABLE sloppiness OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE ERROR_QUIET RESULT_VARIABLE rc)

+        string (REGEX REPLACE "^," "" sloppiness "${sloppiness}")

+        set_target_properties (${target} PROPERTIES CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER "env;CCACHE_SLOPPINESS=${sloppiness};${launcher}")
+    endif ()
+endfunction ()
```

issue.title: Update the zstd fork and evaluate the pending upstream decompression work

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Compression/encoding codecs (LZ4/ZSTD/etc.), archive formats (tar/zip/7z), codec selection and IO...

issue.body:
### Why

`ZSTD(3)` is now the default compression codec of MergeTree columns, marks and primary keys, so zstd decompression is the largest part of many scans. For example, in `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT SearchPhrase) FROM hits` (ClickBench Q5) with the radix partitioned `uniqExact` of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/123552, `ZSTD_decompressSequences` is 51% of the CPU (55% with the other zstd functions), the aggregation itself is 29%, and decompressing the `SearchPhrase` column alone takes 0.050 s of the 0.075 s of the query (32 threads, Zen 4, hot run).

Our fork (`contrib/zstd`, branch `clickhouse` of https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd) is upstream `dev` as of 2025-04-14 (`d654fca7`) plus:
- Unwind information in `huf_decompress_amd64.S` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd/pull/1, https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd/pull/2). Merged upstream as `80cac404` and `a480191f`.
- Vectorized small-offset overlapping copies with NEON `tbl` and SSSE3 `pshufb` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd/pull/3, https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd/pull/4). Proposed upstream as https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4718, still open.

Upstream has not released since v1.5.7 (2025-02-19); `dev` is at v1.6.0-dev and carries a year and a half of changes we do not have.

### The columns cache changes what this buys

The columns cache (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/96844, merged 2026-10-04) keeps deserialized columns of wide `MergeTree` parts in memory, so a repeated read of hot data skips decompression altogether. It is off by default (`use_columns_cache = 0`), and https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/123890 enables it by default after the 26.10 release, sized to 10% of the RAM (`columns_cache_size_to_ram_ratio`) unless `columns_cache_size` is configured. Once it is on, zstd decompression leaves the hot runs of benchmarks whose working set fits in the cache (ClickBench's second and third tries on a large enough machine), and the zstd speed matters for: the first run, data that does not fit in 10% of the RAM, compact parts and tables in `Ordinary` databases (the cache covers neither), and merges, which read and write every part. All measurements in the next section predate the merge of the cache: the branch of #123552 and the master binary used as its reference were both built from a master before 2026-10-04, so none of them has the setting.

Measured separately with the master CI build `0ca8150d9b1d` (26.10.1.1716), same machine and table, `columns_cache_size` 12.5 GiB, `use_columns_cache` 0 vs 1, medians of 21 hot runs; a cached run of Q5 reports `ColumnsCacheHits` equal to `SelectedMarks` (12564) and 46 compressed bytes read, so the cache serves everything:

| Query | 32 threads, cache off / on | 16 threads on 8 cores, cache off / on |
|---|---:|---:|
| `SELECT count() FROM hits WHERE NOT ignore(SearchPhrase)` | 0.051 s / 0.048 s | 0.103 s / 0.052 s |
| `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT SearchPhrase) FROM hits` (master, without #123552) | 0.176 s / 0.163 s | 0.312 s / 0.240 s |
| `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT UserID) FROM hits` (master) | 0.164 s / 0.172 s | |

The first run with the cache on, which fills it, is 1.8x slower than without the cache (0.188 s vs 0.107 s for the `SearchPhrase` scan on 8 cores). With the cache on, the profile of the plain scan is 40% `memcpy` and 33% `ColumnString::insertRangeFrom`: a read copies the cached column into the column of the query. On 32 threads that copy takes as long as decompressing `ZSTD(3)` (both are limited by the memory bandwidth here), so the cache gains nothing on a plain scan of this machine, while on 8 cores, where decompression is CPU-bound, it halves the scan. The decompression speed and the cache are therefore alternatives for the hot runs on machines with few cores per gigabyte of data, and both are irrelevant to a plain hot scan on this machine.

### What has been measured so far

All numbers below are from one machine (AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D, Zen 4, AVX-512), a non-LTO local build of the branch of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/123552, ClickBench `hits` (100M rows) re-inserted with the current defaults (`ZSTD(3)`, one part), medians of 21 runs. "16 threads" is pinned to 8 physical cores like the CI performance tests, "32 threads" is the whole machine. Each row compares against the previous one.

| Variant | `SELECT count() FROM hits WHERE NOT ignore(SearchPhrase)` 16 / 32 threads | same with `URL` | Q5 with #123552 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| upstream `dev` 2026-10-06 (`49cf5179`) + the fork patches, vs the current fork | 1.02x / 1.00x | 1.01x / 1.00x | 1.00x / 0.99x |
| + https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4733 (keep the repeat offsets in registers on x86-64) | **1.13x / 1.11x** | **1.11x / 1.08x** | **1.08x / 1.09x** |
| + https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4751 (sequence decoding rewrite), on top of #4733 | 1.02x / 1.00x | 1.01x / 1.03x | 1.02x / 1.01x |
| + https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/3828 (more prefetching), on top of #4733 instead of #4751 | 0.99x / 0.98x | 0.99x / 0.99x | 0.99x / 0.97x |

The rebase of the fork patches onto upstream `dev` had one trivial conflict (`ZSTD_copy8` in `lib/common/zstd_internal.h`). `#4733` and `#3828` applied cleanly, `#4751` applied with a 3-way merge. A checksum of all columns of `hits` (`sum(cityHash64(*))`) is identical with and without `#4751`.

Nothing has been measured on Intel or on ARM, on other datasets, for compression, or with the columns cache.

### Candidates

Merged upstream since our base (`lib/` only, excluding build and documentation changes):

| Commit | Area | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `cc101959` decompress: sink nextState/nbBits loads in `ZSTD_decodeSequence` | decompress, all | included in the "upstream dev" row above |
| `cbbc114e`, `942937f3` BMI2 dispatch overrides and fallback aliases | decompress, x86 | we compile with BMI2 (`x86-64-v3`), check that the dispatch is resolved at compile time |
| `b89e8c2a` skip the CPUID probe in `CCtx` when BMI2 is enabled at compile time | compress, x86 | |
| `a28e8182` Improve `ZSTD_decodeSequence` performance; `33618c89` revert of its branch optimization; `0dffae42` remove 32-bit code | decompress, AArch64 | |
| `bd38fc2c` struct access in Huffman decode 2X; `1e9d2006` better block copy8 | decompress, AArch64 | |
| `07cd78d3` Neon and `2849f3a5` SVE2 `convertSequences_noRepcodes`; `7e4937bc` SVE2 histogram | compress, AArch64 | SVE2 is not in our ARM baseline, check what is compiled |
| `ae703425` elide the long-offset path on 64-bit; `0055ce7a` simplify sequence resolution in `zstd_opt` | compress, all | |
| `c6f91a41` fix OOB read/write in the DDict hashset probe | correctness | we do not use dictionaries, verify |
| `cef5a561` fix unintended high memory usage; `3a3c506b` fix #4553 | correctness | |
| `38cce026`, `f818f97b` legacy format support disabled by default | format | check `ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT` in `contrib/zstd-cmake` |

Open upstream PRs with performance claims:

| PR | Area | Claim | Measured here |
|---|---|---|---|
| https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4733 | decompress, x86-64 | +5.5% to +9.3% decode with clang on Zen 5 | 1.08x to 1.13x, see above |
| https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4751 | decompress, all | +19% to +23% decode throughput | 1.00x to 1.03x on top of #4733 |
| https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/3828 | decompress, all | prefetching | 0.97x to 0.99x |
| https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4813 | decompress, AArch64 | sequence decoding | not measured |
| https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4715 | decompress, AArch64 SVE | SVE paths | not measured, SVE is not in our baseline |
| https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4718 | decompress, all | our overlap-copy patches | already in the fork |
| https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4646 | compress | level 6 parameters | not measured, we default to level 3 |

### Plan

1. Rebase the fork: create a branch of https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd from upstream `dev`, cherry-pick the overlap-copy patches (the unwind-info patches are upstream already), and bump `contrib/zstd` in a ClickHouse PR. Check `contrib/zstd-cmake` against the upstream build changes (legacy support, `ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT`, the new BMI2 dispatch macros).
2. Verify the bump alone, before any pending PR, on every build in CI (sanitizers included) and with the performance comparison. Compressed output changes are acceptable only for compression; decompression must be bit-identical, checked with a checksum of every column of the test datasets.
3. Evaluate the pending PRs one at a time on top of the bump, with A/B runs of the same binary layout (same compiler, same flags): https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4733 first, then https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4751 and https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4813. Keep a PR only if it is a measured win on both x86 and ARM, or a win on one and neutral on the other.
4. Decide for each kept PR whether to carry it in the fork while upstream reviews it, and comment with the measurements upstream.

What to measure, for each variant against the previous one:
- Everything twice, with `use_columns_cache = 0` and `use_columns_cache = 1` (the default after #123890). With the cache on, report the first run and the repeated runs separately: the first run and the data larger than the cache are what the decompression speed still affects. The single-column tests below must run with the cache off, or they measure the cache instead of zstd.
- Decompression of single columns, with no other work: `SELECT count() FROM t WHERE NOT ignore(col)` for a short string column, a long string column (`URL`, `Title`), a numeric column with few distinct values (`EventTime`, `RegionID`) and a numeric column with many (`WatchID`), and the full-table `SELECT sum(cityHash64(*))`.
- Compression: `INSERT ... SELECT` of the same tables, time and compressed size, plus `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL`, with the default `ZSTD(3)` and with `ZSTD(1)` and `ZSTD(9)`, plus the `codecs_*` performance tests. Merges are not served by the columns cache, so this is where decompression speed keeps mattering once the cache is on.
- End-to-end: the ClickBench queries over `hits` (Q5 with and without https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/123552), TPC-H SF10 and TPC-DS SF1 (the CI performance datasets), and the `system.*_log` tables of a server after a stateless test run, which are a different kind of data (many short strings, `LowCardinality`, `Map`).
- Marks and primary key reads: `ZSTD(3)` is their codec, so cold `SELECT` with a selective primary key condition on a table with many parts.

Where:
- x86: an AMD Zen 4 (what was used so far) and an Intel machine (CI performance tests run on both), with the CI binary (`x86-64-v3`, LTO) rather than a local build.
- ARM: Graviton (NEON, the CI performance tests), the modern profile (`armv8.2-a+crypto`).
- The sanitizer builds for correctness (MSan found an uninitialized read in the first version of the overlap-copy patch).

Closes: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/129680


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Expanding a sparse `String` column to a full one (for `GROUP BY`, `JOIN`, sorting and most functions) now copies its values in one pass, which makes such queries over mostly-empty `String` columns up to 10% faster.

### Description

A part stores a `String` column as sparse when at least `ratio_of_defaults_for_sparse_serialization` (0.9375) of its values are empty. Turning it into a full column (`ColumnSparse::convertToFullColumnIfSparse` and the sparse path of `IFunction`) calls `createWithOffsets`. `ColumnVector` and `ColumnNullable` override it; `ColumnString` did not, so the generic `IColumn::createWithOffsets` inserted every value with a virtual `insertFrom` and every run of defaults with `insertManyFrom`, growing `chars` as it went.

`ColumnString::createWithOffsets` sizes the result once. With an empty default the value bytes are copied with one `memcpy` and the offsets are written in one pass; with a non-empty default (a function result such as `s || 'x'`) each row is copied as `insertFrom` does. Every position is checked before it is written. `Nullable(String)` gets it through `ColumnNullable`. `FixedString` and `Decimal` columns still use the generic implementation. The algorithm is the one proposed in #129680.

Local release build, ClickBench `hits` (100M rows, `MobilePhoneModel` 94% empty and sparse), change [95% CI] over 8 / 4 ABBA pairs:

| Query | 8 threads | 1 thread |

### Description

```sql
INSERT INTO d1.t1 SELECT if(number % 10 < 7, toString(10000000 + cityHash64(number) % 9990000000), toString(1000000000000000000 + cityHash64(number) % 8000000000000000000)) FROM numbers(80000003);
SELECT uniqExact(c1) FROM d1.t1
SETTINGS compatibility = '25.8', max_threads = '8';
```

### Performance

Original query (milliseconds; SQL omitted):

| OLD 26.8.1.672 | NEW 26.10.2.142 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1114 | 2378 | 2.13× |

issue.body:
The ThinLTO release builds (`amd_release`, `arm_release`, `amd_cfi`) are PIE since #117449 / #119284. The runtime cost of PIE vs. non-PIE has never been measured for `amd_release`, and #117449 reported only "one slower entry in three of six batches" for `arm_release`. This issue is about measuring it. It does **not** propose changing the segment alignment: 2 MiB alignment (#125949) stays closed because it reduces the ASLR entropy of the executable base.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/117449
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/119284
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125949
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/126977

Measurements wanted:
1. **Code generation cost.** A draft PR, not meant to be merged, that links the ThinLTO release builds as non-PIE again (the pre-#117449 `-fno-pie` / `-no-pie` branch), run through Performance Comparison on `amd_release` and `arm_release` (a maintainer has to add `can be tested` and `ci-performance`). Since #126977 both servers run with ASLR disabled, so this isolates the cost of PIE code itself. Report the geomean and the queries that are slower or faster beyond the usual thresholds.
2. **Load-address variance with ASLR enabled.** Outside of CI, on one amd64 and one aarch64 machine: the same binary started many times (e.g. 20 starts) with ASLR enabled, running a handful of the queries that #125278 flagged (`logical_functions_small` #15, `multiif` #1, `decimal_parse` #0, `join_squashing_blocks` #0), for the PIE and the non-PIE binary. Report the spread (min / median / max) per query, to separate PIE placement effects from test noise.

comment.body:
🤖 Closing: the runtime cost of PIE has been measured, it is minimal, and we accept it. The release binaries stay PIE.

- amd64 (#127948): query geomean non-PIE / PIE is 1.0004, no measurable difference on queries.
- aarch64 with the same veneer form on both sides (#129828): geomean 0.9895, so PIE costs about 1%.
- `clickhouse_client_startup` and `clickhouse_local_startup` are about 20 to 25% faster without PIE on both architectures. This is a startup cost, also accepted.
- `numbers_with_step` (22% faster without PIE in #129828) is not a PIE effect: on aarch64 its time moves between 208 and 277 ms across master builds that are all PIE, and #127948 showed the opposite sign.

issue.title: GCS INSERTs with s3_create_new_file_on_insert fail for files over 32 MiB

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Object storage connectivity (S3/GCS/Azure) including credentials, retries, multipart, etc.

issue.body:
### Describe what's wrong

- Every INSERT to GCS with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` fails once the object exceeds `s3_max_single_part_upload_size` (32 MiB default).
- Triggered by any INSERT producing a multipart upload, even the first write to a fresh key, no concurrent writer needed.
- Expected both INSERTs to succeed and write two separate numbered files.
- On an `S3` table the later `SELECT` then 404s on the key that was never written.

Root cause: `StorageObjectStorageSink` sets `object_storage_write_if_none_match = "*"` for every backend except HDFS, so `WriteBufferFromS3::preFinalize` throws for a GCS client whenever the upload must go multipart, a guard added separately for small Iceberg metadata objects.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `StorageObjectStorage::write` -> `StorageObjectStorage::createSink` passes `fail_if_exists = create_new_file_on_insert && !truncate_on_insert` (StorageObjectStorage.cpp:1109; partitioned path: StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:198). The sink then sets `object_storage_write_if_none_match = "*"` for every backend except HDFS (StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:76-77). On finish, `StorageObjectStorageSink::finalizeBuffers` -> `WriteBufferFromS3::finalizeImpl` -> `preFinalize`, which throws for a GCS-provider client whenever a conditional create is not a single PUT (WriteBufferFromS3.cpp:188-192).

Affected locations:
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:76`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8a8d2e477fc/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp#L76) — conditional write requested for every backend but HDFS
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp:1109`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8a8d2e477fc/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp#L1109) — createSink passes fail_if_exists for create_new_file_on_insert without truncate
- [`src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:198`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8a8d2e477fc/src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp#L198) — partitioned sink passes the same fail_if_exists
- [`src/IO/WriteBufferFromS3.cpp:188`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/8a8d2e477fc/src/IO/WriteBufferFromS3.cpp#L188) — GCS client throws on a conditional create that is not a single PUT

Impact: On master, every GCS export or append with `s3_create_new_file_on_insert = 1` that produces a file larger than 32 MiB fails, even with no concurrent writer. This worked on 26.10. The error does not point to the workaround (`s3_max_single_part_upload_size` above the file size, which buffers the whole object in memory). Unreleased: neither change is on 26.3/26.8, and 26.10.3.7 writes the files.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master`; not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

Reach MinIO under the hostname storage.googleapis.com so the S3 client detects the GCS provider, then INSERT roughly 40 MB of data to exceed the single-part upload size.

```bash
import pytest

from helpers.cluster import ClickHouseCluster

cluster = ClickHouseCluster(__file__)
node = cluster.add_instance("node", with_minio=True)

@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def started_cluster():
    try:
        cluster.start()
        # The S3 client deduces the GCS provider from the endpoint, so reach MinIO under the GCS host name.
        node.exec_in_container(
            ["bash", "-c", f"echo '{cluster.minio_ip} storage.googleapis.com' >> /etc/hosts"],
            privileged=True,
            user="root",
        )
        yield cluster
    finally:
        cluster.shutdown()

def test_create_new_file_on_insert_multipart_gcs(started_cluster):
    url = f"http://storage.googleapis.com:{cluster.minio_port}/{cluster.minio_bucket}/gcs_new_file"
    creds = f"'{cluster.minio_access_key}', '{cluster.minio_secret_key}'"
    # About 40 MB, more than `s3_max_single_part_upload_size`: the object is uploaded in parts.
    insert = f"INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3('{url}.csv', {creds}, 'CSV', 's String') SELECT repeat('a', 1000) FROM numbers(40000)"

    node.query(insert)
    node.query(insert, settings={"s3_create_new_file_on_insert": 1})

    assert node.query(f"SELECT _file, count() FROM s3('{url}*.csv', {creds}, 'CSV', 's String') GROUP BY _file ORDER BY _file") == "gcs_new_file.1.csv\t40000\ngcs_new_file.csv\t40000\n"
```

### Expected behavior

Both INSERTs succeed and the SELECT lists `gcs_new_file.csv` and `gcs_new_file.1.csv` with 40000 rows each.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
Both INSERTs succeed and the final SELECT returns:
gcs_new_file.1.csv	40000
gcs_new_file.csv	40000
(26.10.3.7 writes `export.csv` and `export.1.csv` with 40000 rows each for the same INSERTs.)
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The second INSERT throws S3_ERROR: GCS conditional create must be a single PUT, CompleteMultipartUpload ignores preconditions.

Actual output of the reproducer above:

```
helpers.client.QueryRuntimeException: Client failed! Return code: 243, stderr: Received exception from server (version 26.11.1):
Code: 499. DB::Exception: Received from 172.18.0.6:9000. DB::Exception: GCS conditional create of gcs_new_file.1.csv must be a single PUT. CompleteMultipartUpload ignores preconditions.. Stack trace:
[frames 0-3 trimmed]
5. src/IO/WriteBufferFromS3.cpp:189:15: DB::WriteB
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

Two options:
- Treat a GCS client like HDFS when the upload goes multipart: fall back to an unconditional `CompleteMultipartUpload` for the `*_create_new_file_on_insert` sink instead of throwing. Trade-off: large GCS files lose the overwrite protection #114995 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) adds, which is the 26.10 behaviour.
- Exclude GCS in the sink altogether. Trade-off: small GCS files also lose the `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0` single-PUT protection.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- If both #114995 and #128866 are backported, the regression goes with them.
- Other S3-compatible stores that reject `If-None-Match` on PUT or CompleteMultipartUpload would now fail these INSERTs too. Could not verify: only MinIO and the GCS client path were exercised.

Found during automated review of [PR #114995](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/114995); this finding was not executed, so nobody is tagged. Per git blame, that PR introduced the cited lines (src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorage.cpp:1109, src/Storages/ObjectStorage/StorageObjectStorageSink.cpp:198). Severity P2 · Finding `h_pr114995_001`

issue.title: Update the zstd fork and evaluate the pending upstream decompression work

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Compression/encoding codecs (LZ4/ZSTD/etc.), archive formats (tar/zip/7z), codec selection and IO...

issue.body:
### Why

`ZSTD(3)` is now the default compression codec of MergeTree columns, marks and primary keys, so zstd decompression is the largest part of many scans. For example, in `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT SearchPhrase) FROM hits` (ClickBench Q5) with the radix partitioned `uniqExact` of https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/123552, `ZSTD_decompressSequences` is 51% of the CPU (55% with the other zstd functions), the aggregation itself is 29%, and decompressing the `SearchPhrase` column alone takes 0.050 s of the 0.075 s of the query (32 threads, Zen 4, hot run).

Our fork (`contrib/zstd`, branch `clickhouse` of https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd) is upstream `dev` as of 2025-04-14 (`d654fca7`) plus:
- Unwind information in `huf_decompress_amd64.S` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd/pull/1, https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd/pull/2). Merged upstream as `80cac404` and `a480191f`.
- Vectorized small-offset overlapping copies with NEON `tbl` and SSSE3 `pshufb` (https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd/pull/3, https://github.com/ClickHouse/zstd/pull/4). Proposed upstream as https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/4718, still open.

Upstream has not released since v1.5.7 (2025-02-19); `dev` is at v1.6.0-dev and carries a year and a half of changes we do not have.

### The columns cache changes what this buys

The columns cache (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/96844, merged 2026-10-04) keeps deserialized columns of wide `MergeTree` parts in memory, so a repeated read of hot data skips decompression altogether. It is off by default (`use_columns_cache = 0`), and https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/123890 enables it by default after the 26.10 release, sized to 10% of the RAM (`columns_cache_size_to_ram_ratio`) unless `columns_cache_size` is configured. Once it is on, zstd decompression leaves the hot runs of benchmarks whose working set fits in the cache (ClickBench's second and third tries on a large enough machine), and the zstd speed matters for: the first run, data that does not fit in 10% of the RAM, compact parts and tables in `Ordinary` databases (the cache covers neither), and merges, which read and write every part. All measurements in the next section predate the merge of the cache: the branch of #123552 and the master binary used as its reference were both built from a master before 2026-10-04, so none of them has the setting.

Measured separately with the master CI build `0ca8150d9b1d` (26.10.1.1716), same machine and table, `columns_cache_size` 12.5 GiB, `use_columns_cache` 0 vs 1, medians of 21 hot runs; a cached run of Q5 reports `ColumnsCacheHits` equal to `SelectedMarks` (12564) and 46 compressed bytes read, so the cache serves everything:

| + https://github.com/facebook/zstd/pull/3828 (more prefetching), on top of #4733 instead of #4751 | 0.99x / 0.98x | 0.99x / 0.99x | 0.99x / 0.97x |

issue.body:
Caused by: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/125001

### Description

uniqExact over a String column with tens of millions of distinct values is much slower on 26.10 than on 26.8. The final merge of the aggregate states regressed: CPU time is about 7x higher at 80M distinct keys and grows faster than linearly with set size, while peak memory roughly halves. Reads and pruning are unchanged.

Regression between `26.8.1.672` (OLD) and `26.10.2.142` (NEW).

### How to reproduce

Run the setup once, then measure only the SELECT on each version.

```sql
CREATE DATABASE d1 ENGINE = Atomic;
CREATE TABLE d1.t1 (c1 String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY c1;
INSERT INTO d1.t1 SELECT if(number % 10 < 7, toString(10000000 + cityHash64(number) % 9990000000), toString(1000000000000000000 + cityHash64(number) % 8000000000000000000)) FROM numbers(80000003);
SELECT uniqExact(c1) FROM d1.t1
SETTINGS compatibility = '25.8', max_threads = '8';
```

### Performance

Original query (milliseconds; SQL omitted):

| OLD 26.8.1.672 | NEW 26.10.2.142 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1114 | 2378 | 2.13× |

Synthetic repro above (milliseconds):

| OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,054 | 7,273 | 6.90× |

Synthetic repro above, peak memory in bytes of the SELECT (`system.query_log`):

| OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 8,129,375,032 | 4,102,637,872 | 0.50× |

### Expected behavior

uniqExact over a large String set should run in about the same time as on 26.8 (about 1.1 s for 80M distinct keys with max_threads=8), not about 7.3 s.

### Additional reproducers

Other findings with the same cause show it in different query shapes (15 findings with their own bisect, on 3 workloads). Each repro is self-contained: run the setup once, then measure only the last `SELECT`.

#### `uniqExact` over about 100M distinct `UUID` values

uniqExact over a UUID column with about 100M+ distinct values is much slower in 26.10 than in 26.8 (no GROUP BY, 8 threads). The time goes into merging the per-thread two-level uniqExact sets (robin-hood shiftCellsRight inside UniqExactSet::parallelizeMergeMulti). Peak memory roughly halves.

```sql
CREATE TABLE default.t1 (`c1` UUID) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple();
INSERT INTO default.t1 SELECT generateUUIDv4(number) FROM numbers(110000000) SETTINGS max_insert_threads = 8;
SELECT uniqExact(c1) AS d, count(c1) AS n FROM default.t1
SETTINGS compatibility = '24.0', max_threads = '8';
```

| | OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Query time, ms | 1,030 | 8,360 | 8.12× |
| Peak memory, bytes | 8,103,994,416 | 4,065,948,688 | 0.50× |

#### `LEFT JOIN` with `parallel_hash` over about 100M distinct `UInt64` build-side keys

A LEFT JOIN whose right (build) side has about 100M distinct UInt64 keys takes about 1.7x longer with the parallel_hash join algorithm on 26.10 than on 26.8, while peak memory halves. With join_algorithm='hash' there is no slowdown.

```sql
CREATE DATABASE d1 ENGINE = Atomic;
CREATE TABLE d1.t1 (c1 String, c2 String) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY c1;
CREATE TABLE d1.t2 (c1 UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY c1;
INSERT INTO d1.t1 SELECT toString(number), toString(cityHash64(number) % 1000000000000000003) FROM numbers(1000);
INSERT INTO d1.t2 SELECT cityHash64(number) % 1000000000000000003 FROM numbers(100000000);
SELECT count(), countIf(p.c1 != 0), countIf(p.c1 = 0) FROM d1.t1 AS a LEFT JOIN (SELECT c1 FROM d1.t2) AS p ON toUInt64OrZero(a.c2) = p.c1
SETTINGS compatibility = '25.8', max_threads = '8', query_plan_join_swap_table = 'false';
```

| | OLD 26.8.36.3 | NEW 26.10.3.7 | NEW/OLD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Query time, ms | 609 | 1,045 | 1.72× |
| Peak memory, bytes | 4,331,482,264 | 2,184,220,152 | 0.50× |

### Description

Draft, not for merge: it repeats the PIE cost measurement of #127948 for #127892, with the aarch64 linker veneers made equal. The `ci-performance` label keeps it unmergeable.

- The first commit is the one of #127948: the ThinLTO RelWithDebInfo builds (`amd_release`, `arm_release`) are linked as non-PIE at the base where the PIE reference is loaded with ASLR disabled, `0xaaaaaaaa0000` on aarch64 and that base modulo 1 GiB, `0x15554000`, on x86-64. `check_executable_base.py` compares the bases modulo 1 GiB.
- The second commit adds `-Wl,--pic-veneer` to the aarch64 non-PIE link. The aarch64 `.text` is larger than the range of a branch, so lld inserts range extension thunks: `ldr x16; br x16; .xword` without PIE, `adrp; add; br` with PIE. With the flag the non-PIE build gets the PIE form. x86-64 has no such thunks and is unchanged.
- The third and fourth commits are the spread run of #127948: both servers start with ASLR enabled, and only batch 1 runs. It restarts both servers 20 times and, after each start, runs `decimal_parse` #0, `join_squashing_blocks` #0, `logical_functions_small` #15 and `multiif` #1 with 15 runs per server. Each restart waits for the old server to exit. The raw data goes to `aslr-spread/` in `logs.tar.zst`; the report and the CIDB uploads are skipped.

Validation on local ThinLTO builds of the first two commits: the aarch64 cross-build has 11,102 `ldr/br/.xword` thunks and 0 `adrp/add/br` thunks without the flag, 0 and 11,102 with it (same counts on the stripped binary); the amd64 build is `EXEC` at `0x15554000` and its link has no `--pic-veneer`. A local spread batch with this PR's amd64 CI build and its PIE reference completed 3 of 3 starts with a new PIE base each time, the non-PIE base `0x15554000`, and every server stop clean.

issue.title: SIGSEGV reading ORC map whose requested key `Tuple` matches no struct field

labels.name: repo-f8f539ca
labels.description: Input/output formats (CSV/JSON/Parquet/ORC/Arrow/Protobuf/etc.).

issue.body:
### Describe what's wrong

- Reading an ORC `map<struct<a:string>,string>` column as `Map(Tuple(A String), String)` crashes the process with signal 11.
- Any key `Tuple` whose names match none of the file's key struct fields triggers it, including a case-only difference at default `input_format_orc_case_insensitive_column_matching = 0`.
- The read should succeed or throw a conversion error; instead it segfaults in `StringDirectColumnReader::next`.
- One `SELECT` with an explicit structure or one `INSERT ... FORMAT ORC` takes the server down; seen on master, 26.10.3.7 and 25.3.14.14.

Root cause: The MAP case of `updateIncludeTypeIds` (`NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp:1210`) does not ensure both key and value add a column id, so an unmatched key `Tuple` selects nothing and the map is built with one child. `createRowBatch` then leaves `elements` null and `MapColumnReader::nextImpl` dereferences it.

<details>
<summary>Analysis details (evidence, affected locations, impact)</summary>

Why we believe this is a bug: `NativeORCBlockInputFormat::prepareFileReader` (`NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp:1318`) -> `updateIncludeTypeIds` MAP case (`:1210-1211`) recurses into key and value separately -> the key's STRUCT branch only recurses into fields found by `findORCStructFieldByName` (`:1228`) and returns (`:1238`) having added no id -> the value adds its id, so `selectParents` (`ORC/Type.cpp:123`) selects the map -> `Type::buildSelectedType` (`ORC/Type.cpp:340-346`) drops the unselected key, leaving a one-child MAP -> `createRowBatch` (`ORC/Vector.cpp:119-126`) builds `keys` from that child and leaves `elements` null -> `MapColumnReader::nextImpl` (`ORC/ColumnReader.cpp:972-977`) reads the value into `*map_batch.elements` -> null dereference (fault address 0x10 in `StringDirectColumnReader::next`).

Affected locations:
- [`src/Processors/Formats/Impl/NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp:1210`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1d607cb1acf/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp#L1210) — MAP case recurses into key and value with no guarantee that each contributes an id
- [`src/Processors/Formats/Impl/NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp:1228`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1d607cb1acf/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp#L1228) — named Tuple element with no matching struct field adds nothing, so a map key Tuple can select nothing
- [`src/Processors/Formats/Impl/NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp:2800`](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/1d607cb1acf/src/Processors/Formats/Impl/NativeORCBlockInputFormat.cpp#L2800) — value-side twin: getSubtype(1) on a one-child MAP throws std::out_of_range

Impact: Server SIGSEGV from one `SELECT` with an explicit structure or one `INSERT ... FORMAT ORC`. Present on master with #130171 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) (in-house ORC reader) and on released 26.10.3.7 and 25.3.14.14 (apache `orc` reader); all three segfault on the same file.

</details>

### Does it reproduce on most recent release?

Confirmed on `master`; not checked on a release.

### How to reproduce

The value-side variant of the same gap throws `std::out_of_range` at `getSubtype(1)` instead of crashing.

```bash
# Tag no-fasttest: ORC is not built in fasttest.

# An ORC map read with a key Tuple that names none of the fields of the file's key struct must not crash.

FILE="$(realpath "$CLICKHOUSE_TMP")/test_repro.orc"
clickhouse-local -q "SELECT map(CAST(tuple('a'), 'Tuple(a String)'), 'v') AS m FORMAT ORC" > "$FILE"

clickhouse-local -q "SELECT * FROM file('$FILE', ORC, 'm Map(Tuple(a String), String)')"
for structure in 'm Map(Tuple(A String), String)' 'm Map(Tuple(b String), String)'; do
    clickhouse-local -q "SELECT * FROM file('$FILE', ORC, '$structure')" > /dev/null 2>&1
    rc=$?
    echo "$structure: $([[ $rc -eq 134 || $rc -eq 139 ]] && echo crashed || echo ok)"
done

rm -f "$FILE"
```

Note: an automated re-run of this exact block on current `master` (`eb580cbadfdf`) did not show the failure; the analyst's run did (outputs below). Environment or ordering may matter.

### Expected behavior

The map is read and the key is converted by `castColumnToRequestedType`, or a normal exception is thrown.

Expected output of the reproducer above:

```
{('a'):'v'}
m Map(Tuple(A String), String): ok
m Map(Tuple(b String), String): ok
```

### Error message and/or stacktrace

The process crashes with SIGSEGV (null dereference at fault address 0x10 in `StringDirectColumnReader::next`).

Actual output of the reproducer above:

```
{('a'):'v'}
m Map(Tuple(A String), String): crashed
m Map(Tuple(b String), String): crashed
```

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

In the MAP case, if the key or the value adds no id, insert that child's `getColumnId()` so it is read whole and `castColumnToRequestedType` converts or throws, the same rule #130171 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) applies to kind mismatches and the UNION case applies to branches. This also removes the acknowledged value-side `std::out_of_range`. Trade-off: the unmatched child subtree is read in full. The case fits into #130171's `05574_orc_requested_type_of_another_kind.sh` rather than a new file.

</details>

### Additional context

Open risks:
- Could not verify debug or sanitizer builds locally: the binary is RelWithDebInfo; the value-side `std::out_of_range` may abort there, as #130171 (where this was found; not confirmed as the cause) body says for the case it fixes.

Found during automated review of [PR #130171](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/130171); whether that PR introduced it could not be established, so nobody is tagged. Severity P1 · Finding `h_pr130171_001`
